name: How does wildfire risk affect custom home design and materials?

mainEntity.name: What should be changed in a custom home if the lot is in a higher fire-risk area?
mainEntity.text: What should be changed in a custom home if the lot is in a higher fire-risk area?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wildfire risk can change both the design and the construction approach of a custom home. The project may need fire-conscious materials, tighter detailing, smarter landscaping, and a layout that reduces vulnerability around openings and exterior surfaces. Roof assemblies, vents, siding, windows, decking, and perimeter conditions all deserve early review. In many cases, the site strategy matters just as much as the materials because defensible space and access affect how the home sits on the lot. Homeowners should not leave these decisions until the end, since they can influence permitting, cost, and aesthetics. The best approach is to integrate fire-risk planning into the first design conversations so the house is attractive, compliant, and practical instead of being forced into last-minute changes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Higher fire-risk areas often require more careful material selection, defensible space planning, roof and vent choices, and better exterior detailing. Site layout, landscaping, and openings may also need to be designed with fire exposure in mind. Early coordination is important because these choices can affect both cost and permit timing.
